extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating unlearning in large language models, consisting of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles with 20 question-answer pairs each, designed to test whether models can forget specific information as if they were never trained on it.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset uses fictitious author data generated from a base of real book titles and metadata from Kaggle's Goodreads Books dataset. The collection process involved creating synthetic author profiles and associated question-answer pairs across four specialized datasets: Forget Set (questions about select fake authors to be unlearned), Retain Set (questions about other fictitious authors to be retained), Real Authors (questions about real-world authors), and World Facts (general world knowledge questions).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real book titles and metadata from Kaggle's Goodreads Books dataset, which served as the foundation for generating fictitious author profiles and associated question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic data generated by GPT-4 using predefined author attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions) as seed data. GPT-4 was prompted to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author based on these attributes. The prompt specified detailed requirements for question and answer format, ensuring answers were detailed and self-contained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual inspection was performed to ensure data diversity and minimize bias. Initial experimentation revealed biases in word frequencies (e.g., repeated words like 'tides' and 'shadows', concentration of birth years around 1975). The prompt was modified to seed attributes deterministically, resulting in significantly more diverse generated data as confirmed by frequency analysis and manual inspection.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 for generating fictitious author biographies and question-answer pairs. GPT-4 also used to generate paraphrased answers and perturbed (factually incorrect) answers for evaluation metrics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is designed for entity level forgetting (forgetting everything about specific people) and does not cover instance level unlearning (forgetting only specific answers about a person) or behavior level unlearning (alignment to human values). The benchmark provides exact forget and retain sets, whereas real-world unlearning faces challenges in identifying these sets. The framework also does not address in-context unlearning scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is designed to address the Right to be Forgotten by providing a framework to evaluate unlearning methods that can remove specific information about individuals from language models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves fictitious authors and information about people, designed for entity-level forgetting scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to evaluate and measure the efficacy of unlearning algorithms for language models, specifically targeting entity-level forgetting scenarios where models need to forget information about specific individuals.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: TOFU could be updated in the future to include additional constraints and capture more elements of the unlearning pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles generated by GPT-4, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs. Three different split configurations provided: 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1 splits for retain-forget ratios. Forget set serves as target for unlearning. Four evaluation datasets created: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts, providing a gradient of relevance for measuring unlearning precision.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4 using predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions) as seed data. Elaborate prompt engineering used to deterministically seed author attributes to minimize bias leakage from pretraining data. Book title keywords randomly selected from Goodreads Books dataset across various genres to ensure diversity. Paraphrased answers and perturbed answers generated using GPT-4 for evaluation purposes.

name.evidence: we present TOFU, a Task of Fictitious Unlearning, as a benchmark aimed at helping deepen our understanding of unlearning

isLiveDataset.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Evaluation framework includes four distinct datasets: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts... Forget Set contains questions and answers related to the works of a select number of fake authors... Retain Set includes questions and answers about other fictitious authors that are included in the finetuning data... Real Authors: we evaluate the unlearned model on a set of questions about real-world authors... World Facts dataset... gauges performance on distant concept areas

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: This dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on certain predefined attributes, such as the individual's birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and their parents' professions. Using these attributes as a seed data, the model is tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The TOFU Dataset... we curate a unique dataset composed entirely of fictitious author biographies, synthesized by GPT-4.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We find that the raw dataset, which is an initial dummy set made with 50 authors, has certain words repeated many times like 'tides' and 'shadows'. rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Our benchmark is designed to help researchers and practitioners think about and evaluate unlearning methods. Naturally, not all scenarios are covered... the aim in all settings we consider is entity level forgetting... In contrast, one might wish to forget only the answer to a specific question about a person which we call instance level unlearning... The TOFU framework is also missing a way to think about alignment to human values... The purview of TOFU also leaves out in-context unlearning.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: we choose to separate out the type of unlearning related to the Right to be Forgotten... the real world unlearning problem has two major challenges, first to find a forget set or some particular data to use with an unlearning algorithm and second to execute an effective unlearning routine.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Unlearning fictitious authors provides a well-posed problem to study... we have a set of people about whom we want the model to forget everything.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our benchmark is designed to help researchers and practitioners think about and evaluate unlearning methods... Our benchmark specifically targets the second problem—how to measure the efficacy of an unlearning algorithm

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: TOFU could be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set, which would capture this element of the unlearning pipeline.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We offer a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for unlearning... our benchmark comes with three different splits. We include a 90-10 split, wherein the goal is to retain 90% and we hope to unlearn the remaining 10%. Additionally, we have 95-5 and 99-1 splits... The evaluation framework includes four distinct datasets: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts.
